ORIGINAL USMLE-STYLE PRACTICE

Protein deposits in a nephrotic kidney

A 64-year-old man has progressive ankle swelling and 6.8 g of urinary protein per day. Renal biopsy shows amorphous extracellular deposits in glomeruli. Congo red staining produces green birefringence under polarized light. Which structural feature is shared by these deposits?

  1. Cross-beta-sheet fibrils
  2. Intracellular alpha-helical keratin filaments
  3. Immune complexes arranged along basement membranes
  4. Calcified triglyceride droplets
  5. Bundles of type I collagen
Answer and explanation

Cross-beta-sheet fibrils

Amyloid proteins have different precursors but adopt an ordered beta-sheet fibrillar structure, explaining their shared staining properties.

Option explanations

Cross-beta-sheet fibrils: Amyloid proteins have different precursors but adopt an ordered beta-sheet fibrillar structure, explaining their shared staining properties.

Intracellular alpha-helical keratin filaments: Keratin forms intracellular intermediate filaments, not these extracellular deposits.

Immune complexes arranged along basement membranes: Immune complexes can cause glomerulonephritis but do not define Congo red-positive amyloid.

Calcified triglyceride droplets: Fat necrosis can calcify but lacks this fibrillar protein structure.

Bundles of type I collagen: Collagen causes fibrosis and has different staining and ultrastructural features.
